userId.description: User id to edit. The /users/{id}/edit route interpolates {id} here so the form targets the named user. Absent (e.g. the self-service /profile screen) → falls back to window.wpAdminWorkspaces.userId (the acting user).

documentation.purpose: Profile editor for the user named by `config.userId` (the acting user, `window.wpAdminWorkspaces.userId`, when `config.userId` is absent). Edits first/last/nickname, display name (chosen from a generated option set), email, website, and biographical info. Reads + writes go through `core-data` `useEntityRecord('root', 'user', userId)`; the save button is disabled until `hasEdits` and shows a loading state while `isSaving`. Success + error route through `@wordpress/notices` snackbar / banner. Covers both the own-profile sub-screen of wp-admin's `users.php?action=editself` flow and (via `config.userId`) the `user-edit.php` edit surface the `core:users` Edit action routes to; the multi-user list lives in `core:users` (`docs/screens/users.md`).

reads.purpose: Profile fields of the edited user (config.userId, else the acting user).
User id to edit (interpolated from the /users/{id}/edit route); falls back to the acting user when absent.
Identify the acting user (fallback when config.userId is absent); absence of both shows a permission-denied message.

writes.purpose: Save accumulated `edit()` calls via `save()` from useEntityRecord.

states.renders: Form with the seven fields populated; Save button disabled.
Same form with Save enabled; dirty-state reported to kernel.
Save button shows loading spinner + disabled state.

interactions.effect: `edit({ name: value })` with options generated from username / first / last / first+last / last+first / nickname / current name.
`await save()`; on success: success snackbar. On failure: error banner with `err.message`.

a11y.focus-management: Form fields are in document order; native focus order is sufficient.

constraints.note: `useEntityRecord('root','user', userId)` returns `{ record: null }` while loading. Reading `record.first_name` without a guard crashes on first paint.

Display name dropdown options are computed in render from the record's name fields. A field combination that produces only one option still renders the select; the user is forced to keep that option even if it's not what they want.

Manifest declares `core:dirty-state: true`. The app does NOT call `useDirtyState` directly — it relies on `hasEdits` being read by a sibling NavigationGuard. (`block-navigation-on-dirty` is intentionally not set; profile edits are low-stakes.)
WPDS `InputControl` onChange takes a DOM event (`e.target.value`), not the raw value. The same applies wherever WPDS form fields are used.
Uses legacy `TextareaControl` from `@wordpress/components` — WPDS 0.12 has no port.
Uses legacy `SelectControl` from `@wordpress/components` for the display name (WPDS 0.12 SelectControl has no `__nextHasNoMarginBottom` parity).

design-system-leakage.purpose: Form layout + text + URL + email inputs + save button.
Bio textarea + display-name select + loading spinner — WPDS 0.12 gaps.
